fixes.explanation: That's what Moses says, baker: “But you who held fast to the LORD your God are alive to this day, every one of you.” Not most of you. Not the lucky ones. EVERY one. Right before that, he says the LORD destroyed all who followed Baal of Peor, a false god (Deuteronomy 4:3). Two groups, two outcomes. And the ones who held on are standing right there listening.

Freedom is a nice guess, but it isn't the reason Moses gives. He says the statutes and ordinances are so Israel “…may live and may enter and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your fathers, is giving you.” Notice who's doing the giving in that verse. It's the LORD. Earning back freedom isn't in it, so the answer is living and taking the land.

Tribes is a good Israel word, but it's not the one on these tablets. Moses says the LORD declared His covenant, “…the Ten Commandments that He wrote on two tablets of stone.” Israel had twelve tribes (Genesis 49:28), and ten commandments, so I get why the numbers got tangled. I'd mix up my own mustache tricks before I'd mix those up twice. Commandments is what fills the blank.

Yes, friend. Moses says the LORD brought them out of Egypt, the iron furnace, “…to be the people of His inheritance, as you are today.” A furnace is a hot, hard place to be stuck. I know a little about being stuck, since I spent years in the back of a junk drawer until an angel called me out. The LORD didn't just open the door for Israel. He took them as His own.

problems.problem: It reuses a line from the Prep cards word for word.
The verse says the LORD is giving Israel the land, but it does not say Israel is not earning anything. That contrast adds a claim the passage does not make.
The statement that there are twelve tribes is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The line about being stuck and someone coming to get him draws on his backstory without identifying the drawer, leaving the comparison unclear to someone who does not know his story.
